Done, and your instinct was exactly right to raise it. Here's the situation now:

**You never need to set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.** Two layers of protection:

1. **No key at all is a fully supported mode** — `ask` returns the ranked, enriched sources (the ledger entries, sessions, and code chunks that answer your question) without any API call. The prose summary on top is optional garnish.
2. **If you do want synthesized answers**, set `GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY` instead (committed in `e61361c`, checked *before* `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). It's a name no other tool reads — Claude Code will never see it, so there's zero risk of your Claude Code sessions silently switching from your subscription to API billing. That risk is real with the global variable, which is precisely why the scoped one now exists and is the documented recommendation.

Cost context for if you ever do enable it: synthesis defaults to Haiku 4.5 with a 1,024-token output cap, so a `git for-ai ask` answer costs a fraction of a cent — but that's your call to make by setting the scoped key, never a default.

One process confession, since honest reporting is the house rule here: my first commit of this change had a TypeScript error in the new test that a piped command masked — the tests passed but the build didn't. I caught it on the immediate re-run and the fix is committed (`6da8a20`); build and all 11 synthesis tests are green.

Still in flight: the review-UI agent. When it lands: verify, commit, wire M12's `ask`/`blame --why`, and then the first real question gets asked of this repo.

Yes on both, with two precise details worth having right:

**1. What `git for-ai review` starts.** It's a Vite-*built* site, not a Vite dev server: the React app is compiled to static assets at build time, and the CLI serves those plus a small JSON API from a plain Node HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1`. From your side it feels identical — run the command, browser opens, site is there — but there's no Vite process, no node_modules-serving dev middleware, no file watching. That's deliberate: the thing a user runs is a finished artifact, and the same build later gets wrapped by Electron unchanged.

**2. Yes, that process picks up the env variable — and the key never leaves it.** The server is a normal Node child of your shell, so it inherits `GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY` from wherever you set it. The flow for an ask from the UI will be: browser → local API → the query engine runs retrieval and calls Anthropic *from the Node process* → prose answer with citations comes back as JSON. The key is never embedded in the page, never sent to the browser, never in any URL — it lives only in the server process's environment. Since the variable name is git-for-ai-specific, you can safely set it at the user level in Windows (System Settings → Environment Variables, or `setx GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY "sk-ant-..."` once) so every future terminal has it — with zero risk to your Claude Code billing.

One sequencing note so expectations match reality on day one: per the spec, the review UI ships with the ask panel visibly present but disabled — the `/api/ask` endpoint gets added when I wire M12 (`ask`/`blame --why` in the CLI), which is the very next item after the review UI lands. So the order you'll experience: `git for-ai review` opens the browsable timeline/detail/session views first, then the ask box lights up right behind it — and since you're setting the key, it'll come up in full AI-analysis mode from its first activation, both in the terminal (`git for-ai ask "..."`) and in the UI.
Let me check whether my shell can see it (processes started before you set it may not have inherited it):

'yes (len ' + k.length + ')' : 'no')" && powershell -c "$v=[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY','User'); if($v){'user-level: set (len ' + $v.Length + ')'}else{'user-level: NOT set'}"

Confirmed — the key is set at user level (right shape for an Anthropic key; I checked existence and length only, never the value). Two practical notes:

1. **New processes get it automatically** — any terminal you open from now on, and therefore any `git for-ai ask` or `git for-ai review` you run yourself, will have synthesis live from the first invocation.
2. **My session's shells started before you set it**, so they don't inherit it. Not a problem: when I dogfood `ask` after M12 lands, I'll read the user-level value into the child process environment at spawn (same no-printing discipline as just now), so the end-to-end live-API test happens under real conditions.

Current state of play, so you know what you're waiting on: the review-UI agent is the last one running. When it reports: I verify and commit it → wire M12's `ask` and `blame --why` (small, mostly rendering over the committed query engine, plus the `/api/ask` endpoint that lights up the UI's ask panel) → then the payoff moment: `git for-ai ask` answering a real question about this repo, with a Haiku-synthesized, citation-backed answer sourced from the intent ledger and captured sessions your machine has been quietly accumulating for three days.
The review UI landed with browser-verified results. Independent verification, then commit:
